The full test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

## Summary

I implemented the email-uniqueness rule in the owner create endpoint (`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`). The V2 controller has no create method, so V1 is the sole `POST /api/owners` handler.

The check lives in the existing email-handling block, right after the email is validated and lower-cased:

```java
String emailKey = email.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
owner.setEmail(emailKey);
boolean emailInUse = this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
    .map(Owner::getEmail)
    .filter(Objects::nonNull)
    .map(existing -> existing.trim().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT))
    .anyMatch(emailKey::equals);
if (emailInUse) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
}
```

Key points:
- Comparison is done on lower-cased (and trimmed) values on **both** sides, so a case-differing email counts as a duplicate regardless of how existing owners' emails were stored.
- It only applies when an email is supplied (email is optional in this app), matching the existing null-guarded email handling.
- Returns **409 Conflict**, consistent with the other conflict rules (telephone-in-use, city cap, household duplicate).

The new `coreRejectsDuplicateEmail` acceptance test passes and the full build is green.
